ui.settings.appearance.window_glass.desc: Lets your desktop show through the app window, blurred by the system. Off by default. Text stays readable on every theme: the slider stops before any theme's text gets hard to read.
ui.settings.appearance.window_glass.rest: Restart Local Operator to apply this change. The window keeps its current look until then.
ui.settings.appearance.window_glass.unsu: Translucent window is unavailable because Reduce transparency is on in your system accessibility settings. Turn it off there and this control will appear.
Translucent window needs Windows 11 version 22H2 or later.
Translucent window is not available on Linux: there is no system blur an app can ask for, and a see-through window without one would show the desktop's text through the app's.
Translucent window is not available on this system.
ui.settings.appearance.window_glass.cove: Which parts of the window go translucent. Sidebars only leaves the conversation and pages solid. Full app also covers them and the side panels; web pages, documents and images shown inside stay solid.
ui.settings.appearance.window_glass.inte: Left is frosted: mostly solid with a hint of the desktop. Right is see-through, as clear as every theme's text allows. Message blocks and cards become tints, inputs keep a firm edge, and code, documents and images stay solid.
ui.settings.appearance.window_glass.mate: The system material behind the app. It also sets how far see-through can go.
